rules.when: The task depends on fresh news, current events, live public facts, or recent market and product changes.
rules.why: Grok is the preferred pool when current web-connected context is central to the work.

rules.when: The task is a trivial mechanical edit such as a rote rename, formatting sweep, targeted typo fix, or simple file gathering.
rules.why: Use the cheapest fast profile when the task is narrow and low ambiguity.

rules.when: The task is an ordinary builder assignment that implements code and was not flagged high tier during intake.
rules.why: The ordinary builder pool. Every member is good enough for this work, so new builder tasks spread evenly across them by round-robin instead of piling onto the first one.

rules.when: The task is a big or ambiguous multi-file feature, a risky refactor, or work that requires holding many moving parts in mind.
rules.why: The high-tier design pool: every member holds this quality floor, and new tasks spread across them by round-robin. The third member shows the disable switch: absent enabled means on, and enabled false removes that member from the pool.
